subject: Action: finalize outbound IP policy & split-horizon DNS for Private Endpoints
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Nimbus Cloud Network Ops <network-admin@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Action: finalize outbound IP policy & split-horizon DNS for Private Endpoints

Hi Mark,

We are preparing to flip traffic for the Redwood Private deployment in us-west-2 and need to finalize the outbound IP authorization and split-horizon DNS arrangement for the private endpoints. I attached our current outbound IP candidate list for your allocation: redwood-egress-ip-list_v3.csv.

Specific asks:
- Confirm the final set of IPv4 addresses/CIDRs we should publish to customers as allowed egress addresses.
- Confirm whether you can provide PTR records (reverse DNS) for each address.
- Proposed TTL and how you recommend running split-horizon during the rollout (we prefer low TTLs early).
- Confirm if TLS termination will happen at your edge or if you can pass-through TLS to the customer gateway.

CC'ing Vivek (infra) and Neha (security) for operational and audit constraints. I've also attached a proposed firewall rules patch which is intended to be applied on customer-facing gateways.

We'd appreciate a confirmation or a tracker link to capture the work and any constraints.

Thanks,
—
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-egress-ip-list_v3.csv (csv), proposed-firewall-rules.patch (patch)

From: Mark Jenkins <network-admin@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Action: finalize outbound IP policy & split-horizon DNS for Private Endpoints

Vanessa,

Thanks for the note — we can NAT egress for the Private deployment and allocate from the candidate list, but we need to reserve a subset for failover and monitoring. Operational answers below: 

- Allocation: we can offer three /29s for us-west-2 (one active, one standby, one for monitoring/health). If that works we'll assign specific IPs and hand them off.
- PTR/Reverse DNS: yes, we can provision PTR records for each IP; we need the hostnames to be provided by you.
- Split-horizon: we can serve split-horizon from our authoritative DNS for the region, or we can provide glue records so you host it; operationally we recommend we serve it for simplicity.
- TTL recommendation: 60s during rollout; increase to 300s after cutover.
- TLS: we support both TLS termination and pass-through. If you plan to do end-to-end TLS to customer gateways, we need the SNI hostnames ahead of time.

Ticket created to track work: https://nimbuscloud.example/tickets/NC-4821

On Mon, Nov 20, 2026 at 09:12 -0800 Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [original message quoted]

Mark Jenkins
Nimbus Cloud — Network Ops

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Jenkins <network-admin@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Action: finalize outbound IP policy & split-horizon DNS for Private Endpoints

Mark — thanks. A few follow-ups and constraints from our side so we can finalize firewall inbound/outbound rules for customer handoffs:

1) IP allocation: three /29s is fine. Please assign deterministic IPs and share a CSV we can drop into customer firewall templates.

2) Reverse DNS: we'll provide hostnames. We prefer reverse entries pointed at redwood-inference.net subdomains so our logging matches service names.

3) NAT behavior: we need stable 1:1 mapping from internal egress session to outbound IP for auditability (no per-packet port-randomization that breaks logging). Can you guarantee sticky SNAT for session durations?

4) Split-horizon: we prefer Nimbus to serve authoritative split-horizon for the short-term rollout; please set initial TTL=60s. We'll review moving to our authoritative DNS after stabilization.

5) Firewall patch: attached proposed-firewall-rules.patch includes the exact port/protocol ACLs we intend to publish to customers. The main change is explicit egress to your assigned IPs on ports 443 and 853 (DoT) and to our ops endpoints on 5222 for internal-messaging telemetry.

If you can confirm the sticky SNAT and provide the final CSV and PTR assignments, we can start scheduling customer notifications.

Thanks,
Vanessa

Attachments: proposed-firewall-rules.patch (patch)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Mark Jenkins <network-admin@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Action: finalize outbound IP policy & split-horizon DNS for Private Endpoints

Mark/Vanessa — quick security checklist before we sign off from Compliance: 

- Auditability: We require egress mapping logs that show customer VPC/private endpoint -> outbound IP mapping (timestamped, session id, internal src). Logs must be retained for 180 days and exportable via S3.
- Key management: If Nimbus will terminate TLS, we need confirmation of HSM/KMS usage for private keys and a key rotation policy.
- SOC2 evidence: provide attestation that egress IPs are isolated per customer tenancy and that there are SLA clauses for network segregation.
- DNS integrity: for split-horizon we require DNSSEC or signed zone transfer between Nimbus and Redwood if Nimbus is authoritative.
- Incident escalation: include a 24/7 pager rotation for production egress incidents and an agreed SLAT for failover.

Please respond with a short attestation and the ticket link to attach to our auditor package. If some items require contract updates, queue with Legal (copied).

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Mark Jenkins <network-admin@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Action: finalize outbound IP policy & split-horizon DNS for Private Endpoints

Vanessa/Neha — quick status update and confirmations. Apologies for the delay; work was gated behind internal capacity but we pushed changes this morning.

- Final IP assignment (us-west-2):
  * 54.187.120.200/32 (active)
  * 54.187.120.201/32 (standby)
  * 54.187.120.202/32 (monitoring)
  CSV attached: redwood-egress-ip-list_v3-final.csv (contains PTR hostnames).

- PTR records: provisioned for the three IPs under reverse.redwood-inference.net.
- SNAT: sticky SNAT for session duration is enabled by default on the egress gateway; 4-hour session stickiness documented in NC-4821.
- TTL: zones provisioned with TTL=60s; we will coordinate a change to 300s after 72 hours of stability.
- TLS: we can pass-through TLS or terminate. For termination we store keys in our KMS (HSM-backed) and can provide rotation certs on 90-day cadence.
- Logs & retention: session mapping logs are exported to the S3 bucket you provided and retained for 180 days; NC-4821 contains the export schedule.
- Ticket and docs: https://nimbuscloud.example/tickets/NC-4821
  Shared design folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxyz-redwood/egress-design

Please confirm acceptance of the three final IPs and we'll publish the change window to affected customers.

Regards,
Mark Jenkins
Network Operations — Nimbus Cloud
Attachments: redwood-egress-ip-list_v3-final.csv, split-horizon-dns-diagram.png
